refinement_suggestions: Narrow the target cohort to users who have watched ≥3 episodes of the same series within the last 7 days AND whose last session ended mid-episode or at a series cliffhanger (detected via completion rate <95% or post-credits cut). Exclude users with >3 distinct in-progress titles, since the algorithm cannot confidently surface a single 'most likely' title for multi-show jugglers — show them the legacy rail instead. This directly addresses the wrong_cohort weakness by restricting the Smart Resume hero to users where a single-title prediction is high-confidence.

Replace the irreversible 'remove the Continue Watching rail' mechanism with a progressive disclosure pattern: the Smart Resume hero occupies the top slot, but the full Continue Watching rail is immediately visible one scroll-down below (not hidden behind 'More options'). The 'More options' expander is removed entirely. This eliminates the hidden_guardrail_risk flagged by agents — users who disagree with the algorithm's pick are never more than one swipe away from their full watch history, preventing the catastrophic 'I can't find my show' failure mode.

Redefine the primary success metric from engagement rate on the Smart Resume hero to 'time-to-first-play from app open' with a guardrail on Continue Watching rail engagement drop. Specifically: the hypothesis passes only if median time-to-first-play decreases by ≥15% for the target cohort AND the 7-day retention rate does not decline by more than 2pp versus control. This addresses the broken_mechanism weakness — the current hypothesis has no falsifiable metric that distinguishes 'faster resume' from 'users gave up finding their show.'

result_full.metric_lift_relative: Treatment converts directionally higher than control on 24 paired identities; the paired-bootstrap interval straddles zero (not separable). Synthetic conversion is a weak behavioral signal — read as rank/direction, not as a calibrated effect size. NOTE: one or more personas in this run lack per-persona behavioral seeds (a v1.0-class pack), so cross-persona variance is degraded — a flat or non-separable metric here may reflect collapsed agent variance rather than a true null effect. Rebuild the pack to v1.1 to de-attenuate. NOTE: only 24 paired identities — below the ~30 needed for the paired bootstrap to separate a moderate effect, so this non-separable result is INCONCLUSIVE (the panel cannot detect an effect of plausible size), NOT evidence of no effect. Increase agents per arm to power the comparison.
